Use Backpack for browser and mobile wallet activity on Gorbagana. Use local keypairs for CLI work, deployments, and scripts.

## Choose the right wallet

Use different signing setups for different jobs.

<ReferenceList columns="two" items={[
  {
    label: "Backpack",
    value: "Browser and mobile wallet",
    description: "Use for app testing, user transfers, bridge activity, and wallet-signed frontend transactions.",
    copy: false,
  },
  {
    label: "Local keypair",
    value: "~/.config/solana/id.json",
    description: "Use for CLI commands, scripts, program deployments, and controlled test wallets.",

  {

    value: "Separate keypair",
    description: "Use a separate authority for production programs instead of reusing a daily wallet.",
    copy: false,
  },
  {
    label: "Explorer",

    description: "Use as the source of truth for balances, signatures, accounts, and program activity.",
  },

Confirm these before you sign transactions.

| Check | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| RPC endpoint is Gorbagana | Transactions must be sent to the right network |
| Wallet has native GOR | You need GOR for transaction fees |
| Recipient address is correct | SVM addresses are irreversible once submitted |
| Transaction opens in the explorer | The transaction landed on Gorbagana |

## Backpack

Use Backpack when you need a wallet popup, mobile wallet, bridge destination, or app signer.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Open Backpack

Install or open Backpack, then select the account you want to use on Gorbagana.

</Step>
<Step>

### Select or add Gorbagana

If Gorbagana appears in the network list, select it. If it does not, add a custom Solana RPC endpoint with:

```text
https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Fund the address

Bridge GOR from Solana to the Backpack address with the [Bridge](/docs/network/bridge).

</Step>
<Step>

### Verify the balance

Search the Backpack address in the [Explorer](/docs/network/explorer). The explorer is the source of truth if the wallet UI is stale.

</Step>
<Step>

### Send a small test transaction

Send a small transfer before using larger amounts or signing through a new app.

</Step>
</Steps>

After you sign, open the transaction in the [Explorer](/docs/network/explorer) and confirm the status.

<Callout type="warn" title="Check the network before signing">
  A Solana-style address can exist on multiple SVM networks. Confirm the app, wallet, or script is using Gorbagana RPC before you sign.
</Callout>

## Scripts and keypairs

Use a local keypair with the Solana CLI when you deploy programs or run scripts.

```bash
solana config set --url https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf
solana config set --keypair ~/.config/solana/id.json
solana address
```

Fund this exact address with native GOR before you deploy or send transactions.

Use a separate keypair for production deployment authority when the program needs controlled upgrades.

<Callout type="warn" title="Do not ship keypairs">
  Keep local keypair files out of frontend apps, repositories, logs, screenshots, and support messages. Browser apps should ask the connected wallet to sign.
</Callout>

## App wallets

For frontend apps, connect Backpack through a Solana wallet adapter flow, then send transactions through a Gorbagana `Connection`.

```ts
import { Connection } from "@solana/web3.js";

const connection = new Connection("https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf", "confirmed");
```

Do not assume a connected wallet is on the correct network. Show the network, sender, recipient, amount, and fee payer before the user signs.

## What to show in your app

Show enough context for the user to understand the signature request.

| Field | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Network | `Gorbagana` |
| RPC | `https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf` |
| Sender | Connected Backpack address |
| Recipient | Destination wallet or program account |
| Amount | Native GOR amount |
| Explorer link | Transaction URL after submission |

## Common issues

<Accordions type="single">
<Accordion title="Backpack shows no balance">

Search the Backpack address in the explorer. If the explorer shows funds, reconnect Backpack, reload the app, and confirm the selected network or custom RPC endpoint.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The app reads a different balance than the CLI">

Compare the browser wallet address with `solana address`. Backpack and the CLI may use different keypairs even when both point at Gorbagana RPC.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The transaction does not appear in the explorer">

Confirm the app or script used `https://rpc.gorbagana.wtf`. If you have a signature, search the exact signature first, then search the sender address.

</Accordion>
<Accordion title="The wallet rejects signing">

Reconnect Backpack, refresh the page, and retry with a small transfer. If the transaction was already submitted, search the signature before retrying.

</Accordion>
</Accordions>
